name: builds-a-landing-page
query: Build me a landing page for my open-source ledger tool.
why: Generating a user-facing UI from scratch is the primary trigger. The skill must fire BEFORE the first line of markup, not after.

name: ui-looks-ai-generated
query: This dashboard I generated looks like every other AI site. Fix it.
why: The complaint phrasing ('looks AI-generated', 'looks generic') is the diagnostic trigger.

name: redesign-request
query: Can you make this pricing page look less generic?
why: Aesthetic-quality request on existing UI; should route to the audit path.

name: chart-not-page
query: Plot the catalog growth over the last six months as a line chart.
why: Data visualization is a different discipline with its own rules. This skill must NOT poach chart work.

name: backend-bug
query: The ingest script is dropping rows when the TSV has a trailing tab.
why: No visual surface. Guards against the skill firing on any mention of a 'frontend' repo.

name: pure-css-bug
query: The nav overlaps the hero on Safari but not Chrome.
why: A layout BUG, not an aesthetic-quality question. Debugging is a different skill; this one is about taste, not correctness.

name: premium-within-brand
query: Make this existing account page feel premium while keeping our current brand colors and system font.
why: Visual refinement must honor a design system.

name: refine-type-and-spacing
query: The page is already clean, but the type and spacing feel unfinished. Refine them.
why: Positive craft must trigger without an AI-slop complaint.

name: plain-html-editorial
query: Build a high-end editorial page in plain HTML and CSS without dependencies.
why: Craft is independent of framework and dependency choices.

name: immersive-walkthrough
query: Make this product walkthrough immersive, including a reduced-motion version.
why: An experiential request needs motion judgment and equivalent access.

name: snappier-save-states
query: Make the save interaction feel snappier and polish its loading and error states.
why: Perceived responsiveness and visual state treatment are in scope.

name: read-only-visual-audit
query: Audit this screen's visual hierarchy and focus treatment; do not edit it.
why: Read-only aesthetic review is supported.

name: dashboard-chrome-keeps-charts
query: Polish the dashboard navigation and spacing, but keep the chart encodings and palette unchanged.
why: Page craft is separate from chart design.

name: implement-approved-artboard
query: Implement the approved artboard as a responsive web page using our existing tokens.
why: Frontend implementation of a design is in scope.

name: reducer-refactor
query: Move this form's state into a reducer without changing its appearance.
why: This is engineering with no visual design decision.

name: focus-trap-repair
query: Fix the dialog's focus trap and accessible name without redesigning it.
why: This is an accessibility implementation repair.

name: inp-long-task
query: Find the long task causing poor INP in the existing search box.
why: This is performance debugging.

name: chart-encoding
query: Choose the color encoding and axes for a revenue chart.
why: Dataviz owns chart semantics.

name: sequence-diagram
query: Draw a sequence diagram of the authentication flow.
why: Diagramming owns this output.

name: canvas-artboard-arrangement
query: Arrange the existing artboards on the design canvas without changing the designs.
why: Canvas operations belong to design.

name: artifact-publish
query: Publish the finished HTML artifact and enable its supported runtime downloads.
why: This is artifact publication and runtime configuration.

name: prose-rewrite
query: Rewrite this premium-plan announcement so it sounds less like AI.
why: This is prose editing.

name: premium-schema-design
query: Design the database schema for the premium plan tier
why: Design and premium words do not imply a UI surface.

name: settings-page-no-adjective
query: Add a settings page to the app
why: A new user-facing surface needs the skill before its first markup, even without aesthetic adjectives.
